question: In which of the following shapes is the famous Sun Temple at Konark designed?
solution:
The correct answer is __**A gigantic chariot**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sun Temple at Konark** is located in the state of **Odisha, India**, and is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**. It is one of the most famous temples in India dedicated to the Sun God.
 
• It is designed in the shape of **a gigantic chariot**, symbolizing the **chariot of the Sun God Surya**. The temple features twelve pairs of elaborately carved stone wheels, which represent the chariot wheels.
 
• The temple was constructed in the **13th century** by King **Narasimha Deva I** of the **Eastern Ganga dynasty**. It stands as a testament to the architectural brilliance of that era.
 
• The chariot is drawn by **seven horses**, representing the seven days of the week. Each horse symbolizes a day, emphasizing the Sun's movement throughout the week.
 
• The intricate carvings on the temple depict various aspects of life, including flora, fauna, deities, and celestial beings. The wheels also act as **sundials**, showcasing the advanced understanding of astronomy in ancient India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Symbolism of the Chariot:**

 
 
• The chariot design signifies the movement of the Sun across the sky, as believed in Hindu mythology. The **seven horses** pulling the chariot represent the seven colors of the rainbow and the seven chakras in the human body.
 
• The twelve pairs of wheels symbolize the **12 months of the year** and the concept of time.
 
 
 
• **Architectural Features:**
 
 
• The temple follows the **Kalinga style** of architecture, characterized by its ornate carvings, towering spires, and intricate sculptures.
 
• The main sanctum (now in ruins) was constructed to align with the first rays of the rising sun, highlighting the temple's astronomical precision.
 
 
 
• **Other Options:**
 
 
• **Lotus Flower:** While the **lotus flower** is a significant motif in Indian art and architecture, it is not the design of the Sun Temple at Konark.
 
• **Circular Stupa:** Stupas are structures associated with Buddhism and are not relevant to the Sun Temple's design.
 
• **Reclining Deity:** This refers to a deity lying in a reclining position, which is commonly associated with temples dedicated to Lord Vishnu, such as the Ranganathaswamy Temple in Srirangam.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO Recognition:**
 
 
• The Sun Temple at Konark was inscribed as a **World Heritage Site** by UNESCO in **1984** for its outstanding universal value and architectural significance.
 
• It is also known as the **"Black Pagoda"** due to its dark-colored construction materials, which served as a landmark for sailors navigating the Bay of Bengal.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The Sun Temple at Konark is part of the **Golden Triangle** of Odisha tourism, which includes **Puri** and **Bhubaneswar**.
 
• The temple is frequently celebrated in literature, art, and dance, with the **Konark Dance Festival** held annually to showcase India's classical dance forms.
 
• It is considered a masterpiece of ancient Indian architecture and is a source of inspiration for modern-day architects and historians.
 
• The temple's construction techniques and astronomical alignments continue to be studied by experts worldwide.
